title: Flowing and Freezing: Correlative Operando Liquid Cell Electrochemistry and Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Nanoscale Liquid-Solid Interfaces
content: Understanding nanoscale processes at liquid-solid interfaces is crucial for improving the performance of various energy storage systems like batteries. Directly observing these interfaces at high resolution length scales under realistic conditions has proved challenging due to their complexity, dynamic behaviour, and often the involvement of sensitive elements such as lithium (Li). Processes like dendrite growth and solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation in Li based battery systems have remained elusive in terms of detailed compositional and structural insights at high resolution length scales, despite significant research efforts [1-3]. This can primarily be attributed to a lack of high-resolution characterisation techniques which are compatible with both the liquid and solid component of these interfaces and those which can capture a dynamic system in its state of interest at high resolutions.
